results.methods:

- Equity-accounted hybrid bond of about EUR 0.7bn. This figure is from memory, not the fetched data.
- Minority interests of EUR 0.16bn.
- Pension and other long-term employee liabilities of about EUR 0.3bn. This is my estimate from an EUR 0.8bn "other non-current liabilities" line, not a disclosed figure.
Equity comes to EUR 2.3-4.0bn, or about EUR 7-12.5 a share. The result is very sensitive to the multiple given leverage near 3x.

Method 2, normalised earnings multiple: latest-twelve-month net income is EUR 374m (EPS 1.16); the five-year average is about EUR 420m (EPS 1.30). After a hybrid coupon of about EUR 33m (estimated), EPS is about 1.05. At 5.5-8.5x that gives about EUR 5.8-9. The multiple is low because free cash flow (about EUR 0.31 a share) converts only about 30% of earnings during the fibre build and does not cover the dividend.

The range blends the two, weighted toward earnings and cash flow.
results.earnings_base_note: Latest twelve months to Q3 2026: net income EUR 374m against a five-year average of about EUR 420m (2021-2025: 443, 450, 357, 447, 398). results.one_line: Proximus is worth about EUR 5.5-9.5 a share (midpoint 7.5) against a price of EUR 6.31, based on 4.4-5.3x FY2026 underlying EBITDA of about EUR 1.85bn less about EUR 5.8bn of debt, hybrid, minorities and pensions, cross-checked at 5.5-8.5x normalised EPS of about EUR 1.05. results.methods:
Trading and reporting currency are both USD, so no conversion. AX is the ordinary common share of a US bank holding company (not an ADR). Share count about 56.7m (market cap / price, consistent with 56.76m basic weighted shares in the 10-Q for the quarter to 2026-09-30; diluted 57.6m). No preference shares, no minority interest, no dividend. Seen in the FMP statements only: no change in share count suggesting a split or rights issue, and buybacks are small (treasury stock up about $14m in the quarter). I did not open the filings or search for pending takeovers.

Method 1, normalised earnings multiple: normalised diluted EPS of $8.40 (see earnings base note) at 9x to 11.5x gives $76 to $97. The multiple is a regional-bank range, held below the top end because the loan book is concentrated in commercial real estate and specialty lending and the stock's beta is 1.3.

Method 2, tangible book value and return on equity: equity $3,289m less goodwill and intangibles of about $272m gives tangible book of $3,017m, or $53.2 per share (stated book $58.0). Justified price-to-tangible-book = (ROTCE - g) / (CoE - g). Low case 14% ROTCE, 11.5% cost of equity, 3.5% growth gives 1.31x, or $70. Central case 16%, 11%, 4% gives 1.71x, or $91. High case 17%, 10.5%, 4% gives 2.0x, or $106.

The range of $76 to $102 blends the two methods; the midpoint of about $89 is my best estimate. Debt is funding for a bank, so it is not deducted separately; the equity methods already sit after all liabilities. FMP shows no capital lease obligations, and I did not check for a pension deficit.
results.earnings_base_note: Latest twelve months to 2026-09-30: net income $507.7m (129.6 + 124.9 + 124.7 + 128.4), diluted EPS about $8.78, return on average equity about 16-17%. Five-year average diluted EPS (FY2022-FY2026: 3.97, 5.07, 7.66, 7.43, 8.48) is $6.52; the gap reflects book value compounding with no dividend, not a margin spike, since ROE has held in the mid-to-high teens throughout. From memory, not checked against the filing, FY2024 included a one-off gain on an FDIC loan purchase, which is why FY2025 dipped. I normalised EPS to $8.40, about 4% below the latest twelve months, to allow for a net interest margin and credit costs that are both better than a through-cycle level. The FY2027 Q1 goodwill and intangibles split in FMP looks reclassified ($271.5m all in goodwill), so I used the combined figure.
results.one_line: Axos is worth about $76 to $102 per share (midpoint about $89) against a price of $87.90, so it looks roughly fairly valued. That rests on normalised EPS of $8.40 at 9-11.5x and tangible book of $53.2 per share at 1.3-2.0x for a 14-17% return on tangible equity.

results.methods:

Share count: 12,404.7m ordinary shares in issue, unchanged in the period. That figure includes about 327m held by the employee share trust. I treated three instruments as converted or exercised because they are well in the money: the 2028 Alat CB (1,667m shares at HK$9.37, removes US$2.0bn of debt), the 2029 CB (421m shares at HK$8.37, removes US$0.45bn), and the Alat warrants (1,230m shares at HK$11.51, which bring in about US$1.81bn of cash). The 2033 CB converts at HK$35.74, is out of the money, and stays as debt. That gives about 15.72bn fully diluted shares. No splits or rights issues; a US$225m CB buyback in June 2026.

Earnings: reported results are losses (Q1 -609m, Q2 -640m) because of non-cash warrant revaluation losses of US$1.7bn and about US$1.9bn. I removed those and used the company's adjusted attributable profit. By quarter: Q3 FY26 589m, Q4 FY26 559m, Q1 FY27 1,075m, Q2 FY27 1,361m. That makes the latest twelve months US$3.58bn, against a run-rate of about US$4.9bn on the last two quarters. The five-year average is only about US$1.65bn (FY22 to FY26: roughly 2.0, 1.6, 1.0, 1.44 and 2.05bn). Revenue is up 48%, driven by the AI-server boom, and component costs are rising, so I did not capitalise the run-rate. I normalised to US$3.2-3.8bn, which is about the twelve-month figure.

Method 1, earnings multiple: 10-13x normalised profit, plus US$1.8bn of warrant cash, divided by 15.72bn shares. That gives about HK$16.8-25.5.

Method 2, EV/EBIT: twelve-month adjusted EBIT of about US$5.1bn at 8-10x. From that I deducted US$4.5bn of debt left after conversion (notes 2.05bn, short-term loans 0.48bn, 2033 CB 2.0bn), plus leases, pension, minority interests and the NCI put of about US$1.8bn. I added US$6.1bn of cash and the warrant proceeds. That gives about HK$21-26.

I blended the two methods and set the range at HK$16.5-25. Analyst targets were not used.

results.one_line: On normalised profit of US$3.2-3.8bn (twelve months US$3.58bn, against a five-year average of about US$1.65bn) at 10-13x, cross-checked at 8-10x EV/EBIT, Lenovo is worth about HK$16.5-25 per share, midpoint about HK$20.8. ACT0.DE is the same ordinary share, quoted at EUR 145.8 for a market cap of about EUR 1,467m, which implies about 10.06m shares. The weighted share count in Q3-26 was 10.08m, down from 10.18m in 2023 because of a small buyback. There was no split, rights issue or takeover in the last 24 months; I used 10.07m shares.

Earnings base:
- LTM net income is about EUR 65.0m (Q4-25 16.7 + Q1-26 18.0 + Q2 16.8 + Q3 13.5), or about EUR 6.45 a share.
- LTM EBITDA is about EUR 116m (company-reported 9M-26 EBITDA of 93.2 plus about 23 for Q4-25). FY26 guidance, reconfirmed 29 Oct 2026, is about EUR 126m.
- The five-year average EPS (2021-25) is only EUR 4.14 (2.72, 2.97, 3.40, 5.31, 6.28). That rise is structural (specialty mix: creatine, nitroguanidine for defence; EBITDA margin up from about 15% to about 21%), not a cyclical spike, so I did not mean-revert to the five-year average. I also did not capitalise the FY26 guidance or the 2027 capacity additions. Normalised EPS is about EUR 6.3-6.45.
- No material one-offs found.

Method 1, P/E: 18-24x on EUR 6.45 gives EUR 116-155 a share.

Method 2, EV/EBITDA: 10-12x on EUR 116-126m gives EV of EUR 1,160-1,510m. From that I deducted:
- Net cash/debt of about zero: Q3 cash EUR 63.8m against about EUR 41m of bank debt and EUR 3m of leases at FY25; 9M FCF was -20m and a dividend and buyback were paid.
- Pensions of about EUR 85m (a broker note cites 88m).
- Minorities of about EUR 2m.
That leaves equity of about EUR 1,075-1,425m, or EUR 107-141 a share.

Customer-funded grants (about EUR 88m of non-current deferred income) are not counted as debt, but they explain why EBITDA overstates free cash during the capex cycle.

Blended range: EUR 110-148 a share, midpoint about EUR 129.
results.earnings_base_note: LTM EPS of about EUR 6.45 (net income 65m) and LTM EBITDA of about EUR 116m, against a five-year average EPS of EUR 4.14. The gap is structural mix and margin gains, so I used LTM rather than the average, and did not capitalise FY26 guidance (EBITDA 126m) or 2027 capacity. The Q3-26 debt and pension split was not available from the filings I could reach, so I estimated it from FY25 and a broker-cited pension figure of about EUR 88m.
results.one_line: Alzchem earns about EUR 6.45 a share on LTM figures and EUR 116m of EBITDA, with roughly zero net debt and about EUR 85m of pensions. That supports EUR 110-148 a share (18-24x earnings, 10-12x EBITDA), midpoint about EUR 129, a little below the EUR 145.8 price.

results.methods:

The five-year average is much worse. 2022-23 had project write-down losses (EBIT -107m and -182m), 2024 EBIT was 88m, and 2025 was 148m. The 2020-21 margin was 3.7-3.9%. So I normalised to a 3.0-3.5% EBIT margin on about SEK 5.8-6.2bn of revenue, giving EBIT of SEK 175-215m and normalised EPS of about 3.05-3.75.

Balance sheet: cash SEK 397m, no bank debt, leases SEK 61m, so net cash is SEK 336m (about 7.4/share). No pension deficit, preference shares or minority interests. Much of the cash is customer advances (SEK 630m deferred revenue), so I counted only about half of it as surplus.

Method 1: P/E of 10-12x on normalised EPS, plus about SEK 3/share of surplus cash, gives about 34-47.

Method 2: EV/EBIT of 8-9x on normalised EBIT of about SEK 195m, plus SEK 170-336m of net cash, gives about 38-46.

Blended range: 34-46, midpoint about 40.
results.earnings_base_note: LTM EPS was 3.98 as reported (about 3.94 at normal tax). results.one_line: On normalised EPS of about SEK 3.05-3.75 (3.0-3.5% EBIT margin on about SEK 6bn of revenue), 10-12x earnings or 8-9x EBIT, plus part of its SEK 336m net cash after leases, gives a value of about SEK 34-46 a share. The midpoint is about SEK 40, slightly above the SEK 36.7 price.

results.methods:
Two methods, both run on normalised adjusted EBIT.

1) Normalised P/E. Net finance cost of about £60m (lease interest included) and a 26% tax rate. Low case: EBIT £300m gives EPS of about 50p, at 17x that is about 845p. High case: EBIT £375m gives EPS of about 65p, at 20x that is about 1,300p.

2) EV/EBIT less net debt. Take normalised EBIT of £330m at 14-16x, which gives an EV of £4.6-5.3bn. Deduct net debt including leases of about £0.93bn (£852m at the March-26 year end, £988m at the seasonal Sep-26 point; this is £579m borrowings plus £940m leases less £531m cash) and £6m of minority interests. That leaves £3.7-4.4bn, or 1,030-1,220p per share.

There are no preference shares, and the pension is immaterial. Share count is about 358m ordinary shares (FY26 weighted 358.3m; market cap divided by price gives 357.7m). There have been no splits, rights issues or takeovers in the last 24 months, and buybacks and the dividend are suspended.

The blended range is 850-1,300p with a midpoint of about 1,075p, roughly 9% below the price.
results.earnings_base_note:

The recovery is not yet proven. H1 FY27 free cash flow was -£147m.

results.methods:
The shares trade in EUR on Euronext Paris and the company reports in EUR, so no currency conversion was needed. Share count is about 137.6m, implied by FMP's market cap of €1,745m at €12.68. That is down from 141.3m weighted average shares in FY26, after €99m of buybacks. There were no splits or rights issues; Pluxee was spun off from Sodexo in February 2024, before the 24-month window.

Earnings base, from the FY26 results to 31 Aug 2026:
- Revenue €1,302m.
- Recurring EBITDA €488m (37.5% margin).
- Reported net income €170m.
- Adjusted net income, Group share, €223m, about €1.59 per share.
- Recurring free cash flow €341m.
- Reported net income over five years: €174m, €81m, €133m, €197m, €170m. The average is about €151m, roughly €1.07 per share.

What I normalised: FY26 is a high point. FY27 guidance is recurring EBITDA of at least €440m, reflecting Brazil's meal-voucher reform and lower interest income on client float. I took recurring EBITDA of about €440m, less roughly €130m of D&A, taxed at about 33%, less minority interests. That gives normalised adjusted net income of about €190-195m, or about €1.40 per share.

Method 1, normalised P/E: 10-12x on €1.40 gives €14.0-16.8. The multiple allows for regulatory risk in France and Brazil and low growth.

Method 2, free cash flow yield (a check): normalised recurring FCF of about €280m, or €2.0 per share, at an 11-13% yield gives about €15.5-18.5.

Deductions:
- The reported net financial cash of €1,341m is NOT added. It is mostly float backing about €4.2bn of vouchers in circulation, and the interest it earns is already in EBITDA and earnings.
- Borrowings of about €1.25bn and leases of €41m are covered by that float.
- Minority interests (€104m at book) are excluded, because both methods use Group-share figures.
- No preferred shares; no material pension deficit.

Result: a range of €14-18 with a midpoint of €16.

results.one_line: On normalised earnings of about €1.40 per share (FY27 guidance of at least €440m recurring EBITDA, down from €488m) at 10-12x, and about €2.0 per share of recurring free cash flow at an 11-13% yield, Pluxee is worth roughly €14-18 a share, midpoint €16, against €12.68 today. The €1.34bn of reported net cash is client float and is not added.

results.methods:
Ambea's pro forma group (Ambea plus Humana, consolidated from 1 Oct 2026) valued two ways, both excluding IFRS 16. Rent is treated as an operating cost, so lease liabilities of SEK 9.45bn are not deducted a second time.
SHARE COUNT: The Q3-26 report gives 80,384,424 shares at 30 Sep, including 5,560,658 held in treasury after a SEK 1.2bn buyback. After the quarter, the treasury shares plus 8,641,622 newly issued shares paid for Humana, taking the total to 89,026,046 ordinary shares with none in treasury. That is the per-share denominator. Trading and reporting currency are both SEK, so no FX conversion is needed.
EARNINGS BASE: Ambea's rolling 12 months to Q3-26: sales 17,247m, adjusted EBITA 1,792m (10.4% margin; 9.6% for FY25), profit 845m, EPS 10.46. Adjusted EBITDA ex-IFRS 16 was 1,624m; less roughly 250m of depreciation on owned assets gives EBITA ex-IFRS 16 of about 1,370m. I add back roughly 60m of one-off items (Humana deal costs of 42m among them), which puts adjusted net income near 895m. Five-year EPS ran 2.51 / 3.89 / 5.07 / 7.21 / 7.95, an average of about 5.3. The rise comes from a structural margin recovery and a falling share count, not a cyclical peak. I therefore use the 12-month figure as the normal base and capitalise no further margin gain.
HUMANA (estimated): net debt ex-leases 1,233m at Q2-26 with leverage of 2.4x, which implies EBITDA ex-leases of about 515m and EBIT ex-IFRS 16 of about 350m. Net income is about 150m. Announced synergies of 120m pre-tax run-rate arrive in year 2; I count them at half to full.
PRO FORMA NET DEBT ex-leases: Ambea 4,369m + Humana 1,233m + cash paid for Humana 932m + Imera 107m + about 70m to buy out the last 2% of Humana ≈ 6.7bn. No preference shares and no material pension deficit.
(1) EV/EBITA ex-IFRS 16 of 12-14x on 1,780-1,840m gives an EV of 21.4-25.8bn. Less 6.7bn net debt, that is 14.7-19.1bn of equity, or SEK 165-215 per share.
(2) P/E of 14-17x on pro forma adjusted net income of about 1,085m (Ambea 895 + Humana 150 − after-tax interest on the 932m cash portion, about 30 + part of the synergies, about 70), which is EPS of about 12.2. That gives SEK 171-207.
Blended range SEK 165-205, midpoint about 185.

results.one_line: After the Humana deal Ambea has 89.0m shares and about SEK 6.7bn of net debt excluding leases. On pro forma EBITA ex-IFRS 16 of about SEK 1.8bn at 12-14x, and adjusted EPS of about SEK 12.2 at 14-17x, the shares are worth roughly SEK 165-205, midpoint about 185, slightly below the 197.9 price.

results.methods: Net asset value (substansvärde), the right method for a listed investment company. I started from the Q3-2026 interim report: NAV was 5,956 Mkr at 30 Sep 2026, or 131 SEK/share on 45,457,814 registered shares. - The board puts the total at about MSEK 5,304, which is about 471m shares. Market cap at SEK 11.06 implies about 465m shares.

Fallback value if the deal fails (Q3 2026 balance sheet):

Range: the HIGH is the SEK 11.25 cash offer, the realistic ceiling with no competing bid. The LOW of SEK 10.5 reflects some deal risk (90% threshold, approvals) and time value. With about 85 to 90% odds of completion, the expected value is about 0.9 x 11.25 + 0.1 x ~8.5, which is about SEK 11.0, close to the midpoint and the current price.

results.methods:

Share count: the Q3-26 report gives 39.29m weighted shares, 40.0m diluted, and share capital of SEK 3.94m at a SEK 0.10 quota value (about 39.4m shares). The count rose from 34.8m to 39.3m over 24 months through directed issues used for acquisitions (Zurvita, It Works!). I used 40m diluted shares. FMP's market cap uses a stale 34.9m share count. No splits, rights issues or takeover bid were found. The B share is the listed ordinary class.

TTM to Q3-26, from company reports:
- Revenue: SEK 3,834m (Q4-25 1,035.3 plus 9M-26 2,799.4)
- EBITDA: SEK 639m (175.2 plus 463.8), a 16.7% margin
- Net income: SEK 456m, EPS about 11.6

Five-year average net income (2021-25) is only SEK 162m, but the business doubled through organic growth and acquisitions, so that average understates today's earnings power. EBITDA margins ran 10-13% historically, and the company's own target is above 11%. The current 17% comes partly from acquisition synergies and a gross-margin jump.

What I normalised: I set the EBITDA margin to 14% rather than 17%, giving EBITDA of about SEK 537m. Less D&A of about SEK 55m and tax at 22%, normalised net income is about SEK 375m, or EPS about 9.4. I found no one-off gains in the reported figures. FMP's operating-line fields are garbled, so I used company-reported EBITDA and net income instead.

Balance sheet: cash SEK 1,019m against debt and leases of SEK 58m, so net cash is SEK 961m. About SEK 930m of other current liabilities are distributor commissions and prepayments, which tie up part of that cash, so I counted only about SEK 500m as excess cash (about SEK 12.5 per share). Minorities are SEK 1.3m, and I found no preference shares or pension deficit.

Method 1, normalised P/E: 10-13x on EPS of 9.4 gives SEK 94-122, plus 12.5 of excess cash, so SEK 106-135.

Method 2, EV/EBITDA: 6-8x on normalised EBITDA of SEK 537m, plus SEK 0.5bn excess cash, divided by 40m shares gives SEK 93-120. At 6-7x on actual TTM EBITDA it gives SEK 108-125.

Blending the two gives SEK 100-130, with a midpoint of about 115.
